title: Momentum Transfer Bowling Lane
description: A concept car sits at one end of a frictionless lane with an array of ShaderBall pins arranged in a triangular formation at the other end. The user adjusts the car's mass, launch velocity vector, and spin, then launches it to collide with the pins, observing conservation of linear and angular momentum in real time. An undo/redo system lets the user step back through parameter changes and re-launch attempts.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a physics bowling simulation. Load CarConcept.glb as the projectile and load ShaderBall.glb six times arranged in a 1-2-3 triangular pin formation on a glossy rectangular lane (50×12 units). Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,18,-30) looking at lane center; add OrbitControls. Lighting: one DirectionalLight with shadows, one HemisphereLight, and a subtle ambient. Physics: implement a simple impulse-based rigid-body system (no library) tracking position, velocity, mass, angular velocity, and rotation for each object. Enforce conservation of linear momentum and kinetic energy (elastic collisions) using 3D sphere-approximated collision detection and response between all objects. Each ShaderBall pin has mass 1. UI panel (HTML overlay, left side): (1) a slider for car mass (1-10), (2) an X-velocity slider (-10 to 10), (3) a Z-velocity slider (5-30), (4) a spin slider for Y-axis angular velocity (-5 to 5), (5) a Launch button that releases the car, (6) a Reset button that restores pins and car to start, (7) Undo and Redo buttons that step through the history of ALL slider changes and launches as discrete states. Display a live HUD (top-right) showing total system linear momentum vector magnitude and total kinetic energy; these values must remain constant (within 1%) after launch to prove conservation laws hold. After launch, animate at 60fps using a fixed-timestep (1/120s) integration loop with sub-step accumulation. Pins knocked beyond lane bounds glow red. The lane surface should have a subtle grid texture generated via canvas. All interactions (slider adjustments, launch, reset) are recorded in an undo/redo stack with a maximum of 50 states. The task requires 10-14 interaction steps: adjust mass, set X-velocity, set Z-velocity, set spin, launch, observe, undo back to change velocity, re-launch, redo, reset, and repeat with different parameters.
